scenarios.title: At the Petrol Station
scenarios.text: A man filling up his motorbike recognises him and starts telling him, in great detail, what he did wrong last Saturday. His little son is hiding behind his leg, staring at {J} like he's a superhero.

choices.label: Listen, then sign the boy's arm
choices.text: He nods through the tactical lecture, then crouches and signs the boy's arm with a marker. The father forgets his criticism entirely.

choices.label: Smile and leave
choices.text: He smiles, says thank you for the advice, and drives off. In the mirror, the boy is waving.

scenarios.title: A Message From {T}
scenarios.text: 'You awake? Can't sleep. Big game Saturday. You?' It's {T}, and it's nearly midnight.

choices.label: Call him
choices.text: They talk for half an hour about nothing: films, food, an old coach. Both of them sleep better afterwards.

choices.label: Reply 'Go to sleep, legend'
choices.text: A thumbs up comes back. Sometimes that's all anyone needs.

scenarios.title: Dinner Is Ready
scenarios.text: {Pf} has cooked his favourite meal, lit a candle and put her phone in a drawer. She looks nervous, like she's going to say something important.

out.text: She just wanted a normal evening with him. That's all. They have one.
She's been offered a job she really wants. They talk about it until midnight.

choices.label: Eat and enjoy it
choices.text: He eats two helpings and tells her it's the best meal he's had all year. She doesn't say whatever it was. Maybe next time.

scenarios.title: Voice Note From {MUM}
scenarios.text: A four-minute voice note from {MUM}: the neighbours, the price of rice, {SIB}'s exams, a dream she had about him scoring, and, at the very end, 'Eat properly.'

choices.label: Send a long voice note back
choices.text: He walks around the flat telling her everything. She replies with eleven heart emojis and a photo of her cooking.

choices.label: Reply with a heart
choices.text: A heart. She sends back 'okay 😊'. Mothers know.

scenarios.title: The Boy at the Gate
scenarios.text: A boy, maybe ten, is waiting at the training-ground gate in a homemade shirt with {J}'s name hand-painted on the back. He's been there since 8am, says the security guard.

choices.label: Get out of the car
choices.text: He gets out, signs the shirt, takes a photo and gives the boy his own training top. The boy's mother cries. So does the security guard, nearly.

choices.label: Wave from the car
choices.text: He waves. The boy waves back like it's the best moment of his life. Maybe it is.

scenarios.title: Player Ratings
scenarios.text: The newspaper's player ratings are out. He got a 4/10. The comment underneath says 'Anonymous. Should be dropped.' He was not anonymous; he was everywhere, badly.

choices.label: Read it and use it
choices.text: He screenshots it and saves it in a folder called 'Fuel'. It's getting quite full.

choices.label: Throw the phone on the sofa
choices.text: The phone bounces off the sofa and onto the floor. The screen survives. His mood doesn't.

scenarios.title: The Neighbours
scenarios.text: The flat upstairs is having a party. It's 1:30am. He has a match tomorrow afternoon. The bass is coming through the ceiling like a second heartbeat.

out.text: They recognise him, apologise and turn it down. One of them asks for a selfie at the door.
They invite him in. He declines. They turn it down slightly.

choices.label: Earplugs and suffering
choices.text: Earplugs, a pillow over his head, and a very long night.

scenarios.title: An Old Photo
scenarios.text: {SIB} sends an old photo: {J} at eight, in a shirt three sizes too big, holding a ball with no air in it, grinning like he's already won something.

choices.label: Post it
choices.text: He posts it. 'Same dream, better ball.' It's the most-liked thing he's posted all year.

choices.label: Set it as your phone background
choices.text: He sets it as his background. Every time he picks up the phone, the eight-year-old reminds him why.

scenarios.title: {BFf} Needs Advice
scenarios.text: {BFf} calls: he's thinking of quitting his job as {BFjob} to start something of his own. He wants {J}'s honest opinion, not the encouraging one.

choices.label: Be honest
choices.text: He asks hard questions about money and plans. {BFf} goes quiet, then thanks him. 'That's why I called you.'

choices.label: Encourage him
choices.text: 'Do it. Life's short.' {BFf} is fired up. Whether it's wise, time will tell.

scenarios.title: The Public Gym
scenarios.text: Early session at a public gym. A man asks for a selfie mid-set. Then his friend. Then the friend's friend. He has eight reps left and a growing queue.

choices.label: Finish the set, then photos
choices.text: 'Two minutes, I promise.' He finishes, then does twelve selfies. Everyone's happy.

choices.label: Photos now, workout ruined
choices.text: Thirty photos later, his muscles have gone cold. He goes home.

scenarios.title: The Delivery
scenarios.text: The delivery driver bringing his dinner is wearing the shirt of {R}, the rival club. He hands over the bag, looks up, and freezes.

choices.label: Make a joke and tip big
choices.text: 'I won't tell anyone.' He tips double. The driver posts about it that night: 'Respect.'

choices.label: Ask for his opinion on the derby
choices.text: They argue happily about the derby on the doorstep for ten minutes. The food goes cold. Worth it.

scenarios.title: On the Massage Table
scenarios.text: The physio, digging into his calf, mentions casually that the manager was asking about {J}'s attitude this week. Just asking. Probably nothing.

choices.label: Ask what exactly he said
choices.text: The physio says the manager just wants to see more hunger. Useful to know.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: He lets it go and enjoys the massage. Mostly.

scenarios.title: Rain
scenarios.text: His day off. It's pouring. His body says stay in bed. A small voice says: the players who make it run in the rain.

choices.label: Run in the rain
choices.text: Eight kilometres in the rain. He comes home soaked and grinning like an idiot.

choices.label: Stay in bed
choices.text: He stays in bed. Rest is training too.

scenarios.title: {SIB}'s Exams
scenarios.text: {SIB} has a big exam tomorrow and is panicking. {SIBhe} calls {J}, of all people, because 'you're good under pressure'.

choices.label: Give the pre-match speech
choices.text: He gives {SIB} his best pre-match speech, adapted for maths. {SIB} laughs, calms down, and passes.

choices.label: Tell {SIBhim} to sleep
choices.text: 'Sleep is the best revision.' {SIB} doesn't believe him. {SIBhe} passes anyway.

scenarios.title: A Like
scenarios.text: {EXFLAME} has liked a photo of his from three years ago. Accidentally? Deliberately? At 11pm on a Saturday?

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: He ignores it. Some doors are better closed.

out.text: She replies: 'Oops. Old photos. Hope you're well.' Polite. Done.
They talk until 3am. It's nice. It's also confusing.

scenarios.title: The Wrong Boots
scenarios.text: In the dressing room before the match, he opens his bag. Two left boots. The kit man is already on the bus back to the training ground.

choices.label: Borrow a teammate's spares
choices.text: A teammate has spares half a size too big. Three pairs of socks later, they fit. Mostly.

choices.label: Call {DAD} to drive them over
choices.text: {DAD} drives across the city in record time and arrives at the players' entrance waving the boot. He's never been prouder to be useful.

scenarios.title: The Lucky Charm
scenarios.text: His lucky bracelet, the one {MUM} gave him before his first trial, has snapped. Big match tomorrow. He knows it's silly. He also knows how he feels.

choices.label: Fix it tonight
choices.text: He spends an hour fixing it with fishing line from a hardware shop. Superstition satisfied.

choices.label: Decide luck is in your legs
choices.text: He puts it in a drawer. Luck is in the legs. He hopes.

scenarios.title: The Cleaner
scenarios.text: The woman who cleans the dressing room after training stops him. Her grandson is a huge fan and is in hospital. She's embarrassed to ask, but would he record a message?

choices.label: Visit the hospital himself
choices.text: He visits on his day off with a signed ball. The grandson doesn't stop smiling for an hour. The cleaner can't speak.

choices.label: Record the message
choices.text: A heartfelt video message. The cleaner plays it for the whole ward.

scenarios.title: Unknown Number
scenarios.text: An unknown number calls three times. Then a message: '{JR} from {OUT}. Just want to confirm a story about you. Call me.'

out.text: The story is wrong and he corrects it. {JRl} thanks him. The article never runs.
The story is right, and now he's confirmed it.

choices.label: Pass it to the club's press officer
choices.text: The press officer handles it. Safe, slow and a little cold.

scenarios.title: Supermarket
scenarios.text: Three women in the supermarket have recognised him and are discussing, loudly, whether he's eating properly. One of them has taken a vegetable out of his trolley and replaced it with a better one.

choices.label: Accept their wisdom
choices.text: He leaves with a trolley curated by three strangers and their phone numbers in case he needs recipes.

choices.label: Politely escape
choices.text: He thanks them and escapes to the frozen aisle. They follow.

scenarios.title: The Challenge
scenarios.text: The fitness coach has set a squad challenge: a hundred push-ups as fast as possible. The current record holder is a forty-second centre-back who won't stop talking about it.

out.text: Forty-one seconds. The squad erupts. The centre-back demands a recount.
Fifty-two seconds and he collapses at ninety-three. Respect, and laughter.

choices.label: Film everyone else
choices.text: He films the attempts. The video of the reserve goalkeeper collapsing at twelve is the best thing on the club channel all month.

scenarios.title: Broken Down
scenarios.text: His car dies on the motorway on the way to training. The tow truck will be an hour. Training starts in forty minutes.

choices.label: Call a teammate for a lift
choices.text: A teammate picks him up, laughing all the way to the training ground. He's three minutes late. The fine is small. The teasing is enormous.

choices.label: Call the manager to explain
choices.text: {Mf} appreciates the call. 'Take a taxi. Don't be late again.'

scenarios.title: A Big Box
scenarios.text: A huge box from {BRAND} has arrived: free products, a handwritten note and a request for 'just one story'.

choices.label: Post a genuine story
choices.text: He posts it honestly. The brand is thrilled. His followers barely notice it's an advert.

choices.label: Give it all to the youth team
choices.text: He gives the whole box to the academy boys. Pandemonium. Better than any story.

scenarios.title: A DM From the Enemy
scenarios.text: {T}, who plays for {R} and has been winding {J} up all season in public, sends a private message: 'Respect for Saturday. You were the best player on the pitch. Don't tell anyone I said that.'

choices.label: Reply with respect
choices.text: 'Respect back. See you in the derby.' Rivals in public, something else in private.

choices.label: Screenshot it for the group chat
choices.text: He screenshots it for his teammates. It leaks within the week. {T} never messages him again.

scenarios.title: Back of the Bus
scenarios.text: On the long coach home from an away match, the back of the bus has started a sing-along. It's terrible. Everyone is singing. The manager is pretending to sleep.

choices.label: Sing louder than anyone
choices.text: He takes the lead on a song from his childhood. By the end, the whole bus knows the words.

choices.label: Headphones and sleep
choices.text: He sleeps through it. Someone draws on his face. Classic.

scenarios.title: Your Usual?
scenarios.text: The barista at {PLACE} has his order ready before he reaches the counter. She also has a small note on the cup: 'Good luck on Saturday 💪'.

choices.label: Leave a big tip and a signed napkin
choices.text: He leaves a big tip and a signed napkin. It's framed behind the counter the next day.

out.text: Her name is {F}. They talk for ten minutes. He's late for training and doesn't care.
She tells him her name and that her boyfriend is a huge fan. Fair enough.

scenarios.title: Grandpa
scenarios.text: His grandfather has learned how to use video calls. He's holding the phone upside down and shouting. He wants to know why {J} isn't married yet.

choices.label: Talk for as long as he wants
choices.text: Forty minutes of the ceiling, half of grandpa's face, and very strong opinions about football in 1974. Wonderful.

choices.label: Promise to visit soon
choices.text: He promises a visit. Grandpa says he'll hold him to it. He will.

scenarios.title: The Imposter
scenarios.text: Someone has made a fake account pretending to be him and is messaging fans asking for money 'for charity'. Three people have already sent some.

choices.label: Warn your followers immediately
choices.text: His warning goes out within minutes. The fake account is reported into oblivion.

choices.label: Refund the victims yourself
choices.text: He finds the three fans and refunds them. They become fans for life.

scenarios.title: The Video
scenarios.text: A father sends a video of his fourteen-year-old daughter's skills. She's genuinely brilliant. There's no girls' academy in their town. He asks if {J} knows anyone.

choices.label: Make some calls
choices.text: Two calls, one email. A women's club academy offers her a trial. The father sends a voice note crying with joy.

choices.label: Share the video
choices.text: He shares the video. Within a day, three clubs have contacted the family.

scenarios.title: 3am Thoughts
scenarios.text: 3:15am. Wide awake. Thoughts about contracts, form, home and whether he left the oven on. The ceiling has no answers.

choices.label: Get up and write it all down
choices.text: He writes every thought on paper. Out of his head, onto the page. He sleeps by four.

choices.label: Scroll the phone
choices.text: Scrolling until 5am. Bad idea, as always.

scenarios.title: The Question
scenarios.text: At a school visit, a small girl puts her hand up: 'Are you scared when you play?' Two hundred children wait for the answer.

choices.label: 'Yes, every time.'
choices.text: 'Yes, every time. Being scared and doing it anyway is called courage.' The teachers write it on the board.

choices.label: 'Never!'
choices.text: The children cheer. The girl looks a little disappointed. She wanted the real answer.

scenarios.title: Her Ex
scenarios.text: At a restaurant, {Pf}'s ex walks in with friends. He nods at {Pf}. She nods back. {J} feels something he doesn't like.

choices.label: Stay relaxed
choices.text: He keeps the conversation flowing. {Pf} squeezes his hand under the table. Nothing to worry about.

choices.label: Ask about him on the way home
choices.text: She answers patiently. Then she asks why he's being jealous. Fair question.

scenarios.title: On the House
scenarios.text: The owner of a small family restaurant refuses to let him pay. 'You make us proud,' he says, and puts a photo of {J} on the wall next to his grandmother's.

choices.label: Accept graciously, come back often
choices.text: He accepts, then comes back every month with teammates who do pay. The restaurant is packed on matchdays now.

choices.label: Insist on paying, tip enormously
choices.text: He leaves money under the plate while the owner isn't looking. The owner chases him down the street. They both laugh.

scenarios.title: Wrong Word
scenarios.text: In the canteen, trying to ask for 'more rice' in the local language, he says something that makes three teammates choke on their food. The chef goes very red.

choices.label: Laugh with them
choices.text: He laughs harder than anyone. The squad adopts the phrase forever. The chef forgives him eventually.

choices.label: Ask what he said
choices.text: They tell him. He wants the floor to swallow him. It becomes his favourite story.

scenarios.title: Photographer Kid
scenarios.text: {KID} has taken his phone and filmed forty minutes of the ceiling, the dog and the inside of a nostril. Also one genuinely beautiful photo of {J} laughing.

choices.label: Post the beautiful one
choices.text: Credited to 'my photographer'. Two million likes. {KID} demands a fee.

choices.label: Keep it private
choices.text: He keeps it. It's on his lock screen for years.

scenarios.title: Room 412
scenarios.text: Team hotel. His key card opens the wrong room. Inside: the manager, in pyjamas, watching a romantic comedy and eating ice cream.

choices.label: Apologise and leave, say nothing ever
choices.text: He leaves. The next day, {Mf} nods at him with an expression that means: never speak of this.

out.text: {Mf} laughs, invites him in for ten minutes, and they bond over a terrible film.
{Mf} closes the door without a word. Sunday training is very hard.

scenarios.title: {MUM} Watched Alone
scenarios.text: {MUM} mentions on the phone, casually, that she watched his last match alone because {DAD} fell asleep and {SIB} was out. She narrated it to the cat.

choices.label: Set up a family watch party
choices.text: He organises a screen, food and the whole extended family for the next match. {MUM} sends twenty photos.

choices.label: Promise to call at half-time
choices.text: He calls at half-time next match. Thirty seconds. She tells everyone.

scenarios.title: Godfather?
scenarios.text: {T} shows him a photo of his newborn son, then asks, very seriously, whether {J} would be the godfather.

choices.label: Yes, honoured
choices.text: He says yes and means it. A tiny person now has his number saved under 'Uncle'.

choices.label: Ask for time to think
choices.text: He asks for a few days. {T} looks a little hurt, then understands.

scenarios.title: A Song About Him
scenarios.text: The ultras have written a song about him. {T} sends the video: two hundred people in a bar singing his name to the tune of a pop song. It's absurd and wonderful.

choices.label: Learn the words and sing it at training
choices.text: He sings it in the dressing room. The squad joins in. Someone posts it. The ultras go wild.

choices.label: Just enjoy it
choices.text: He watches it eleven times. Then sends it to {MUM}, who watches it forty.

scenarios.title: The Wallet
scenarios.text: He finds a wallet on the street with a few notes, an ID card and a photo of a baby. The address is twenty minutes away.

choices.label: Return it in person
choices.text: He returns it himself. The owner, a young father, nearly faints when he sees who's at the door.

choices.label: Hand it to the police
choices.text: He hands it in. The owner gets it back the next day and never knows who found it.

scenarios.title: The Mascot Suit
scenarios.text: The club's mascot performer is sick. The marketing team is desperate: a children's event in an hour, and the suit is roughly his size.

choices.label: Wear the suit
choices.text: He spends two hours as a giant furry animal. Nobody knows. He's never had more fun. Then a child pulls off the head.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: He declines. The assistant kit man does it instead and is a natural.

scenarios.title: Pre-Match Nap
scenarios.text: The team hotel. Three hours before kick-off. His roommate is snoring like a broken engine. He needs this nap.

choices.label: Earplugs and patience
choices.text: Earplugs in. Thirty minutes of half-sleep. Better than nothing.

choices.label: Wake {T} up
choices.text: He throws a pillow. {T} wakes up offended, then laughs. Neither of them sleeps.

scenarios.title: Mini-Me
scenarios.text: A video of a five-year-old perfectly copying his celebration, hairstyle and walk is going viral. The boy's mother has tagged him.

choices.label: Recreate it with the boy
choices.text: He invites the boy to training. They film the celebration together. Forty million views.

choices.label: Send him a mini kit
choices.text: A tiny kit with his name and number arrives at the boy's house. The mother sends the photo. Pure joy.

scenarios.title: Your Old Teacher
scenarios.text: An email from his primary school teacher: 'You were the worst-behaved boy in my class and I knew you'd be someone. I'm retiring next month.'

choices.label: Go to her retirement party
choices.text: He turns up at the retirement party unannounced. She cries. The whole school staff takes photos.

choices.label: Write back a long letter
choices.text: A long letter about the things she taught him that weren't on any exam. She reads it at her party.

scenarios.title: Seat 2A
scenarios.text: On a commercial flight, the crew offer him a free upgrade. In the economy seat next to his is an elderly woman travelling alone, terrified of flying.

choices.label: Give her the upgrade
choices.text: He asks the crew to upgrade her instead. She holds his hand during take-off before she moves forward. A passenger posts about it.

choices.label: Take the upgrade
choices.text: He takes it and sleeps the whole flight. Fair enough.

scenarios.title: The Chant
scenarios.text: In a video from the stands, some of his club's fans are singing a nasty chant about a rival player's family. His name is in the next line of the song.

choices.label: Ask the fans to stop
choices.text: His post asks fans to keep the passion and drop the cruelty. Most agree. Some don't like being told.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: He says nothing. It's not his chant. It's still uncomfortable.

scenarios.title: Sunday Ride
scenarios.text: A cycling group passes his house every Sunday morning: thirty middle-aged men in very tight clothes. Today they've slowed down and are shouting his name through the gate.

choices.label: Join them for an hour
choices.text: He borrows a bike and rides with them for an hour. They talk tactics the whole way. Best recovery session of the month.

choices.label: Wave from the window
choices.text: He waves in his pyjamas. They cheer anyway.

scenarios.title: A Parcel
scenarios.text: A parcel from {Pf}: a framed collage of every match ticket from every game she's watched him play, with a note: 'All of these, and all the ones to come.'

choices.label: Call her straight away
choices.text: He calls her and can't quite get the words out. She laughs at him, lovingly.

choices.label: Hang it where you'll see it every day
choices.text: It goes up in the hallway. He touches it on the way out to every match.

scenarios.title: The Stairs
scenarios.text: The morning after a match, he takes the stairs one at a time, holding the rail, like an old man. His neighbour's kid watches with concern.

choices.label: Ice bath and stretching
choices.text: Ice bath, stretching, foam roller. By lunchtime he's merely stiff.

choices.label: Laugh at yourself
choices.text: 'This is what thirty looks like, kid.' The kid nods seriously.

scenarios.title: The Tattoo
scenarios.text: A fan has tattooed {J}'s face on his calf. It looks a bit like {J} and a bit like a confused goat. The fan is extremely proud and has sent photos.

choices.label: Post it with love
choices.text: 'Best likeness yet.' The fan is famous for a week. The goat jokes are endless.

choices.label: Send him a signed photo to fix it
choices.text: He sends a high-resolution photo 'for the touch-up'. The fan frames the photo instead.
